newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Bund options vol eases, calls unwind.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Bund options vol eases, calls unwind.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options eased back on Friday as investors squared off their positions on December contracts, traders said.
One London-based broker said December volatility was now trading about 4.4 percent, down from 4.52 at the close on Thursday.
December Bund futures were quoted at 100.93 at 1537 GMT, four basis points up on Thursday's close, after setting a new contract high of 101.14 earlier in the day.

Volatility started to ease around lunchtime, but the broker said there was no impact on the market from an earlier report by Germany's independent panel of "wise men" which called for tough budget savings to help Germany meet the Maastricht criteria.
The broker said the Bund volatility will be fairly restrained next week.
"Most people feel the move from here is going to be fairly limited either up or down. Implied volatility if anything will ease back on those expectations," he said.

The same broker gave vol levels for other months at 4.9 percent for January (down from 4.99 percent on Thursday night), 4.94 percent for February, down from 5.00 per cent, and 5.05 percent for March, down from 5.08 percent.
"Mainly we have seen interest in upside calls. People have been selling out of the upside calls after the rallies we have seen over the last week and a bit," said the broker.
"People are unwinding their long positions on the call market and if anything seeing a little bit of activity in downside puts."
One futures and options trader at Chase said the next move for volatility depended on the underlying and whether it could build on its buoyant form to tackle the 101.48 alltime high set in January.
"If it gets up there it is in uncharted territory so unless the mark goes sideways which is unlikely, vol will probably be up again next week," he said.
The Chase trader said the general level of trade in Bund options was "not bad, with good two-way action, but futures were fairly thin".
